data_type: Vector occurrence records (ticks, mosquitoes, biting midges, sandflies)
access_method: GBIF-hosted occurrence search, shapefile download, web viewer
update_freq_desc: Periodic upload to GBIF (interval not published)
temporal_cov_desc: Continuous since 2014; VectorNet in its third phase (2024-2028)
license_type: Not explicitly published on portal (GBIF-hosted; typically CC0/CC-BY)
governance_body: ECDC and EFSA jointly via the One-Health VectorNet Entomological Network (OHVEN)
notes: Joint ECDC/EFSA project since May 2014, now in third iteration (2024-2028). Validated by a network of medical/veterinary entomologists across EU member states and neighbouring countries. SCORING AUDIT: license_openness corrected 1→0 — licence is unstated ("typically CC0/CC-BY" is an inferred platform convention, not a documented licence); applying the unstated-evidence rule (unstated licence scores 0 unless an open licence is explicitly documented) for consistency with SYS08, which already scored 0 for the same situation.

data_type: Species distribution maps (presence/introduced/absent/unknown) for 7 tick species
access_method: Static map files published on ECDC website; historical versions searchable
update_freq_desc: Irregular (evidence shows updates roughly every 1-3 years; latest observed June 2026 vs prior October 2023)
license_type: ECDC copyright/IP notice applies; not an open data license
standards_used: VectorNet network validation; NUTS administrative geography
notes: Covers Dermacentor reticulatus, Hyalomma lusitanicum, H. marginatum, Ixodes persulcatus, I. ricinus, Ornithodoros erraticus, Rhipicephalus sanguineus. Maps state they 'do not represent the official view or position of the countries.' Built on VectorNet (SYS01) validated records. SCORING AUDIT: spatial_resolution corrected 2→1 — evidence is NUTS3/NUTS2 (regional); rubric defines regional=1, point-level GPS=2. license_openness corrected 1→0 — evidence states an explicit ECDC copyright/closed licence, matching the 0-tier (closed/restricted licence). FLAGGED (not rescored, double-counting scan): schema_completeness/semantic_alignment (1,1) and data_quality (2) all draw partly on "VectorNet network validation" language — a borderline case of one evidence source touching three criteria; left as-is pending further review.

operator_org: INRAE (with CPIE Nancy-Champenoux, ANSES, Universite de Lorraine, Tous Chercheurs)
data_type: Citizen-reported tick bite records + physical tick specimens
access_method: "Signalement TIQUE" mobile app, website form, paper form; interactive risk map
update_freq_desc: Continuous citizen reporting since 2017 (no stated batch/publish interval for aggregated data)
spatial_res_desc: Bite location reported per-record; public map shows aggregated risk, not raw points
temporal_cov_desc: Continuous since 2017; >104,000 reports, >60,000 specimens received as of most recent figures
license_type: Not published (no explicit data-sharing/reuse license found)
governance_body: INRAE-led multi-partner consortium; French Ministries of Agriculture/Ecology/Health as supporters
notes: Three components: reporting app, tick specimen library (only one of its kind in Europe per INRAE), and linked database. Produced the first tick-bite risk map of France.

data_type: Research coordination network output (no centralised occurrence dataset)
access_method: Publications, training schools, short-term scientific missions; no shared database
update_freq_desc: Action runs 2022-2026; no data update cycle (coordination network, not a data system)
license_type: Publications generally open access per COST norms; no dataset license (no shared dataset)
notes: A COST Action, not a data portal: coordinates European partner countries applying the DAMA protocol to anticipate tick-borne disease risk. Included here because it is frequently cited alongside data systems in the interoperability literature, but it produces no queryable dataset of its own.

operator_org: RIVM (Netherlands Centre of Expertise on Lyme disease / NLe partners)
data_type: Tick bite + symptom + longitudinal health-outcome reports
update_freq_desc: Weekly participant prompts; continuous data collection
temporal_cov_desc: Multi-year running programme, longitudinal 1-year follow-up per participant
license_type: Not published (no explicit open-data license found)
governance_body: RIVM (Dutch national institute for public health and environment)
notes: Part of the Netherlands Centre of Expertise on Lyme disease. In 2025 recorded the most tick bite reports in five years (6,035 in 2024). Includes longitudinal follow-up for erythema migrans and long-term Lyme outcomes.

operator_org: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) - Centre for Climate and Health Security
data_type: Tick specimen identification records (species, host, location, season)
access_method: Postal specimen submission to UKHSA Porton Down; records published via NBN Gateway; quarterly dashboard
standards_used: NBN Gateway biodiversity data infrastructure (Darwin Core-compatible)
notes: Public, health practitioners, vets and wildlife groups submit specimens; UKHSA provides species ID within ~2 weeks. All records published openly via the National Biodiversity Network gateway. The most mature, professionally documented system in this assessment. SCORING AUDIT: update_frequency corrected 2→1 — evidence (update_freq_desc="Quarterly data releases") matches the periodic (weekly-annual) tier, not continuous/real-time; original score appears to have conflated this with temporal_coverage (system has run continuously since 2005), a separate criterion.

operator_org: ADMED Microbiologie, ZHAW, Zeckenliga (with NRZK, Fondation Sana)
data_type: Individual tick-bite diary entries + specimens sent to national reference lab
access_method: Consumer mobile app (iOS/Android); specimens mailed to NRZK, La Chaux-de-Fonds
update_freq_desc: Real-time risk display to individual users; underlying dataset publication cadence not documented
spatial_res_desc: Per-user location for personal risk display; aggregated/open dataset not documented
temporal_cov_desc: Ongoing app; no multi-year public trend data documented
governance_body: Multi-institution consortium (ADMED, ZHAW, Zeckenliga); no single named governance/oversight body found
notes: Covers Switzerland and Liechtenstein, available in DE/EN/FR/IT. Uses weather + location for a five-level real-time bite-risk score. Specimens can be mailed to the National Reference Centre for Tick-borne Diseases (NRZK), but no public research dataset or API was found. SCORING AUDIT: governance_gdpr_clarity corrected 1→0 — evidence states "no single" named governance/oversight body, which is the rubric's own 0-tier trigger phrase.

operator_org: Robert Koch-Institut (Centre for Artificial Intelligence in Public Health Research) with Observation.org
data_type: Citizen tick/mosquito photographs with AI + expert species identification
temporal_cov_desc: Ongoing initiative (start year not confirmed in source)
license_type: Not published on RKI page (Observation.org data typically flows to GBIF)
notes: AI-assisted species recognition validated by human experts. Focused on tracking climate-driven range shifts of ticks and the Asian tiger mosquito. SCORING AUDIT: license_openness (0) reviewed against the unstated-evidence rule (unstated licence scores 0 unless an open licence is explicitly documented) — already consistent, no change. FLAGGED (not rescored, double-counting scan): schema_completeness (1) is lower than semantic_alignment (2) despite both being drawn from the same "Darwin Core-compatible" standards_used text — worth a separate consistency review outside this audit's scope.

data_type: Tick specimens + pathogen test results (Zecken-Atlas dashboard)
access_method: Postal specimen submission with paper form; public Tableau dashboard
temporal_cov_desc: Builds on RKI standardised collection in Berlin/Brandenburg since 2008, expanded nationwide 2021-2022, ongoing
notes: Initially funded by the Federal Ministry of Health (2021-2022). Citizens 18+ submit ticks and receive feedback; pathogen testing includes TBE virus and Lyme borreliosis agents. FLAGGED (not rescored, double-counting scan): schema_completeness (1) and data_quality (2) both partly draw on "RKI standardised tick-collection methodology" — weak potential overlap; schema_completeness is already conservative (partial, not maximal), left as-is.

data_type: Citizen tick photo/specimen reports (primary target: Hyalomma spp.)
access_method: Email/postal submission; public interactive report map
update_freq_desc: Ongoing since 2021 launch (map update cadence not published)
spatial_res_desc: Interactive map of report locations (public raw-data access not documented)
temporal_cov_desc: Since 2021 (~4-5 years); intensive 2021 campaign (>31,000 site visits in 7 months)
license_type: Explicitly restricted: "information provided will only be used within the research"
governance_body: HUN-REN (Hungarian Research Network) via Centre for Ecological Research
notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: primary target species are the non-native Hyalomma marginatum and H. rufipes, not Ixodes ricinus. I. ricinus specimens are recorded incidentally alongside Dermacentor, Haemaphysalis and Hyalomma finds, so this system's I. ricinus coverage is a by-product rather than its purpose.

operator_org: University of Turku (Tick Project) with Pfizer Oy Finland
data_type: Citizen tick observations via live map
update_freq_desc: Updated daily according to submitted observations
temporal_cov_desc: Continuous since April 2021; >220,000 observations to date
license_type: Pfizer Oy copyright notice; no open license published
governance_body: University of Turku (research) / Pfizer Oy Finland (site maintenance/funding)
notes: Tracks Ixodes ricinus and I. persulcatus per the associated Sormunen et al. research, though the public site itself only says 'ticks'. Commercially co-funded by Pfizer, which is disclosed but not governed by an independent public body. Support inbox states emails 'will not be answered.'

operator_org: Austrian Agency for Health and Food Safety (AGES)
data_type: Tick specimens with Borrelia (and planned further) pathogen testing; also published as a structured occurrence dataset
access_method: Specimen submission programme (national rollout from 2024); records also published via GBIF Integrated Publishing Toolkit as a downloadable Darwin Core Archive
update_freq_desc: Annual reporting and annual GBIF dataset versioning (2025 edition observed)
spatial_res_desc: Point-level records in the GBIF-published Darwin Core Archive
temporal_cov_desc: Launched 2024 as part of the EU OH SURVector project; pathogen scope expanding from 2025
license_type: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) on the GBIF-published dataset
standards_used: Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) via GBIF/IPT; One Health surveillance framework (OH SURVector, RAISE EU projects)
notes: 2024 pilot: 1,420 ticks tested, 87% Ixodes ricinus, 20% overall Borrelia infection rate, with regional variation reported. The OH SURVector project also publishes a structured dataset to GBIF ("National tick surveillance in Austria for the detection of tick-borne pathogens 2025", 8,298 Darwin Core records, CC BY-NC 4.0, GBIF UUID a80d6378-91b9-4075-b349-849e13f1b564) - this materially improves the system's real interoperability profile over what the narrative AGES news articles alone suggest.

data_type: Citizen tick-bite reports (anonymous + registered monthly cohort)
access_method: Website and iOS/Android apps, GPS-coded submissions; dynamic public map
update_freq_desc: Continuous monitoring; registered cohort reports monthly
governance_body: Sciensano (Belgian federal research institute) with AVIQ funding
notes: Trilingual (Dutch/French/German) reflecting Belgium's regions. Combines anonymous crowd reporting with a registered panel for baseline reliability; also runs periodic tick-collection campaigns for pathogen testing. Feeds into prevention-policy risk maps. Species-confirmed via lab identification of submitted specimens: 98.7-99% of TekenNet-submitted ticks are Ixodes ricinus (Philippe et al. 2024, Parasites and Vectors).

operator_org: ANSES, INRAE, SVA, Statens Serum Institut/DTU, WBVR, RIVM (Michelet et al. 2014)
data_type: Laboratory pathogen-screening dataset from field-collected nymphs
access_method: Published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology (open-access journal article), DOI 10.3389/fcimb.2014.00103; no live portal
update_freq_desc: One-time study; sampling conducted 2008-2012, published 2014, never updated since
spatial_res_desc: Six named collection sites across the three countries
temporal_cov_desc: Single study period 2008-2012 (not an ongoing programme)
governance_body: Multi-institutional academic consortium (no ongoing joint governance body post-publication)
standards_used: BioMark microfluidic real-time PCR; results confirmed via Sanger sequencing against GenBank references
notes: 7,050 Ixodes ricinus nymphs pooled into 47 samples across 6 sites; simultaneous screening for 25 bacterial and 12 parasitic species. Included as a landmark example of a rigorous but non-recurring, non-interoperable research dataset, illustrating the gap between one-off academic studies and operational surveillance systems. SCORING AUDIT: schema_completeness corrected 2→0 and semantic_alignment corrected 1→0 — standards_used ("BioMark microfluidic real-time PCR; results confirmed via Sanger sequencing") describes lab-assay methodology, not a data-interoperability schema or shared vocabulary (no Darwin Core/FAIR/shared occurrence schema evidenced anywhere for this system); that same lab-rigour evidence correctly remains the sole basis for data_quality (2), per the double-counting fix.
